slides.title: Cache Mapping Techniques
content: Cache is a small high-speed memory that stores frequently used data to reduce access time between CPU and main memory :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
Direct mapping assigns each memory block to a fixed cache line, making it simple and fast but prone to conflict misses
Associative mapping allows any memory block to be placed in any cache line, reducing conflicts but increasing complexity
Cache mapping improves performance by reducing memory access time and optimizing hit rates

slides.title: Virtual Machines & Spooling
content: A virtual machine is an isolated environment that runs its own operating system using shared physical hardware :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
A hypervisor manages virtual machines by allocating CPU, memory, and storage resources
Spooling stores I/O tasks in a buffer so devices can process them asynchronously without blocking CPU execution
These concepts improve resource utilization, multitasking, and system efficiency

slides.title: Network File System (NFS)
content: NFS is a distributed file system that allows multiple systems to access and share files over a network as if they were local :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
It enables centralized storage, consistent data access, and efficient collaboration
Clients mount remote directories and perform operations transparently
It improves scalability but depends on network performance and reliability

slides.title: Thread Safety & Reentrancy
content: Thread safety ensures that code executes correctly when accessed by multiple threads simultaneously using synchronization mechanisms :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
Reentrancy ensures that a function can be safely interrupted and called again without affecting previous executions
Thread-safe code may use locks while reentrant code avoids shared mutable state
Both concepts are essential for reliable concurrent programming and system stability

slides.title: OS Security Mechanisms
content: Operating system security mechanisms protect system resources from unauthorized access and threats :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
They include authentication, authorization, access control, encryption, and auditing
Techniques like sandboxing and intrusion detection enhance system protection
These mechanisms ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data

slides.title: Future Trends in OS
content: Microkernels minimize kernel size by moving services to user space, improving security and reliability :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
Containers provide lightweight virtualization with shared kernel and isolated environments
Emerging trends include cloud-native OS, serverless computing, and edge/IoT operating systems
Future OS designs focus on modularity, scalability, and efficient resource utilization
